flags.what_is_published: The 2026-11-16 games were nevertheless captured and settled by session arena/aa1d3c07-nba2 (PR #115) reading the official game list directly, so the coverage page now shows 11/16 complete: 8 of 8 finals, 8 of 8 graded. The finding therefore narrows: the pipeline cannot do it unattended, and every future game day will need the same manual capture until the fetch is re-pointed. Two reachable official endpoints exist (www.nba.com/schedule at HTTP 200 and the official gamebook PDFs at HTTP 200) and the repair is a parser against one of them — filed as a suggestion rather than shipped untested, because a parser that returns a wrong official score is worse than a gap that says so.

flags.what_is_wrong: Two committed official result feeds store overtime differently: one appends the OT periods to the quarter row, the other keeps regulation in away_quarters and the extra periods in ot_quarters. Summing the first field alone makes the 2026-11-15 NYK@TOR row appear not to reconcile (95 vs a final of 112).
flags.what_is_published: Both are correct and both are kept. The gate normalises them before checking, and the per-game table prints which schema each row came from. No score was altered.

flags.what_is_wrong: On the settled sample (27 distinct graded games), the model's out-of-sample log-loss is 0.7058 against a coin-flip baseline of 0.6931 — worse than a coin flip. The winner hit rate is still 19/27 (0.704), so the damage is concentrated in confident misses, not in picking sides. The Poisson-binomial tail is p = 0.085, i.e. inside the noise band.
flags.what_is_published: Published, not suppressed. The build does not fail on it — a research desk that gates its own bad news stops being one — and the consequence is stated plainly on the market-prior page: the pre-registered rule now gives the market the entire weight as soon as the market shows any skill, because the model has shown none on this sample. 27 games is a small sample and it is not staked; the bet surface still publishes zero rows.
